recognize_zh: AML 化療中病人皮膚出現中央藍紫色壞死、外圍紅暈的結節（類 ecthyma 病灶），切片可見血管腔內充滿淡染的真菌菌絲並阻塞血管（箭頭），代表血管侵襲性黴菌感染，臨床脈絡下符合播散性鐮刀菌病（fusariosis）。
features: Clinical photograph of a round skin lesion with a central blue-violaceous to necrotic center and a surrounding erythematous rim (panel A)
Dermal/subcutaneous vessel whose lumen is occluded by pale fibrinous material containing numerous fungal hyphae (arrow, panel B)
Thickened vessel wall with sparse inflammatory cells, consistent with angioinvasion and thrombosis
Surrounding collagen/skeletal muscle bundles without a prominent neutrophilic infiltrate, compatible with neutropenia
Hyphal septation and branching angle cannot be reliably assessed at this magnification
describe_en: Clinical photograph shows a well-circumscribed cutaneous nodule with a dusky blue-violaceous necrotic center and an erythematous halo. The skin biopsy shows a deep vessel with luminal thrombosis containing abundant pale-staining fungal hyphae, with angioinvasion and a paucity of surrounding inflammation. Speciation of the hyphae is not possible on H&E alone because Fusarium, Aspergillus and other hyalohyphomycetes appear similar; culture or molecular identification is required. In a neutropenic patient undergoing AML induction, findings are consistent with angioinvasive disseminated mould infection, compatible with fusariosis.

ddx.vs: Aspergillus also forms narrow septate acute-angle branching angioinvasive hyphae, so separation from Fusarium requires culture (banana-shaped macroconidia) or PCR, though positive blood cultures favor Fusarium.
Mucorales hyphae are broad, ribbon-like and pauciseptate with right-angle branching, unlike the narrow septate hyphae of Fusarium.
Ecthyma gangrenosum shows gram-negative bacilli cuffing vessels without fungal hyphae on GMS/PAS stains.
Leukemia cutis shows a dermal infiltrate of blasts rather than intravascular fungal elements and necrosis.
